o1.biggest_strength: It catches the two biggest signals in the data: Monsoon Dark buyers need a match, and ex-subscribers should not be won back until the delivery problem is fixed.
o1.biggest_mistake: It does not put the 46 to 90 day at-risk group first in the main target order, even though that is the cheapest leak to stop.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the 46 to 90 day flow the first programme with its own offer, sequence, draft and value estimate, and add a clearer break-even lift calculation by segment.

o2.biggest_strength: It correctly makes the 46 to 90 day group the first move and clearly calls out the Monsoon Dark and subscription delivery problems.
o2.biggest_mistake: The Monsoon Dark replacement is weak and partly unfinished, and the subscriber track lacks a ready-to-send first message despite being one of the highest-risk segments.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Use a proper closest-match Monsoon Dark track, include the subscriber win-back draft and value, and calculate reach using both email and WhatsApp opt-ins without double-counting.

reason: Output 1 is more complete and ready to run, especially on the subscription gate, message drafts and profit logic. Output 2 has the better first priority with day-68 at-risk customers, but it is less finished where the owner most needs precision.
